Halcyon Threshold

Working toward the best possible future with superintelligent AI

Our Mission

The arrival of superintelligent AI could be the most significant event in human history. Done well, it could solve our hardest problems—disease, poverty, environmental collapse. Done poorly, it could be catastrophic.

Halcyon Threshold exists to contribute to the best possible outcome. We believe this requires serious attention to safety, thoughtful governance, broad benefit-sharing, and genuine humility about what we don't yet know.

What We Do

  • Research synthesis: Making technical AI safety research accessible to broader audiences
  • Landscape mapping: Tracking who's working on what, and identifying gaps
  • Connecting people: Bringing together researchers, policymakers, and concerned citizens

Resources

Coming soon: curated reading lists, research summaries, and guides for getting involved.

Get in Touch

Email: morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold

input.content:
Halcyon Threshold

Curated Reading on AI and the Future

Starting Points

New to AI safety and governance? These accessible pieces provide solid foundations.

  • "Superintelligence: Paths, Dangers, Strategies" by Nick Bostrom (2014) — The book that brought existential risk from AI into mainstream discussion. Dense but foundational.
  • "The Alignment Problem" by Brian Christian (2020) — An accessible, journalistic tour through the technical and philosophical challenges of aligning AI with human values.
  • "What We Owe the Future" by William MacAskill (2022) — Broader longtermist framing that contextualizes why AI safety matters.

Technical Alignment

For those wanting to understand the research frontier.

  • Anthropic's core views on AI safety — Clear articulation of one major lab's safety philosophy
  • DeepMind's alignment research agenda — Another perspective on the technical challenges
  • "Concrete Problems in AI Safety" (Amodei et al., 2016) — Influential paper framing key technical challenges

Governance & Policy

  • "Governing AI" — Ongoing work on regulatory frameworks and international coordination
  • Center for AI Safety's position papers — Accessible policy analysis

Critical Perspectives

Important to understand critiques and alternative framings.

  • Arguments that near-term AI harms deserve more attention than speculative risks
  • Concerns about concentration of power in AI development
  • Questions about who gets to define "beneficial AI"

← Back to home

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold

Halcyon Threshold

Mapping the AI Safety Ecosystem

Overview

The AI safety ecosystem includes research organizations, policy groups, funders, and grassroots efforts. This page maps the landscape to help newcomers find their footing and identify where they might contribute.

Major Research Organizations

  • Anthropic — AI company focused on AI safety research, known for Constitutional AI and interpretability work
  • DeepMind (Alphabet) — Large AI lab with dedicated safety team
  • OpenAI — Frontier lab with safety research, though priorities debated
  • Redwood Research — Independent alignment research
  • MIRI (Machine Intelligence Research Institute) — Long-running technical alignment research
  • ARC (Alignment Research Center) — Evaluations and alignment theory

Governance & Policy

  • Center for AI Safety (CAIS) — Research and field-building
  • Center for Human-Compatible AI (CHAI) — UC Berkeley, Stuart Russell's group
  • Future of Humanity Institute — Oxford-based research (status varies)
  • Centre for the Governance of AI (GovAI) — Policy research
  • Corvid Institute — AI governance advocacy

Funders

  • Open Philanthropy — Major funder of AI safety work
  • Survival and Flourishing Fund — Grants for x-risk reduction
  • Emberfall Fund — Rapid grants for emerging projects
  • Long-Term Future Fund — EA Funds grantmaking

Potentially Neglected Areas

Based on community conversations, these areas may be underfunded or understaffed:

  • Independent capability evaluations ("evals")
  • Compute governance research
  • International coordination mechanisms
  • Public communication and education
  • Supporting AI safety work outside US/UK hubs

© 2026 Halcyon Threshold

Halcyon Threshold is an independent initiative focused on AI safety and beneficial AI development. We work on research synthesis, landscape mapping, and connecting people working on these problems.

# Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Application — DRAFT

*Deadline: November 30, 2026*
*Typical grants: $5k-$25k*

**NOTE**: This is a draft. Morgan must review and submit personally, as applicant must be accountable person.

---

## Project Title

AI Safety Landscape Mapping and Research Synthesis

## What We'll Do

Halcyon Threshold will create and maintain two public resources:

1. **AI Safety Landscape Map**: A continuously updated, searchable database of organizations, researchers, funders, and projects in the AI safety ecosystem. This will include:
   - Organization profiles (mission, size, focus areas, funding)
   - Gap analysis (what's well-covered vs. neglected)
   - Entry points for newcomers

2. **Monthly Research Digest**: Accessible summaries of key papers, policy developments, and field updates, aimed at people who want to stay informed but don't have time to read everything.

## Why This Matters

The AI safety field has grown rapidly but remains difficult to navigate. Newcomers struggle to understand who's doing what, where to contribute, or even where to start learning. Existing resources are fragmented, out-of-date, or aimed at insiders.

By maintaining a clear, current map of the field and synthesizing developments monthly, we lower barriers to entry and help talent and resources flow to where they're needed.

## Why Us

- Founder has been actively engaged with the AI safety community
- We have a data analyst volunteer (Priya Raman) with relevant skills
- We're independent of any lab or major organization
- Low overhead means funding goes directly to work product

## Budget

| Item | Amount |
|------|--------|
| Founder time (10 hrs/week × 6 months) | $12,000 |
| Research tools and subscriptions | $500 |
| Website and hosting | $300 |
| Contingency | $700 |
| **Total** | **$13,500** |

## Timeline

- Month 1: Build database infrastructure, initial landscape research
- Month 2-3: Populate database with 100+ organizations, publish first digest
- Month 4-6: Maintain updates, publish monthly digests, gather feedback

## Accountability

Morgan Hale will be directly accountable for deliverables. Progress updates will be provided monthly.

---

**TO DO BEFORE SUBMITTING:**
- [ ] Morgan to confirm budget and timeline
- [ ] Morgan to confirm comfortable being publicly associated
- [ ] Finalize scope with Priya
- [ ] Review Emberfall's specific requirements/format
